protections: P1: Manager's own trusted state (config.ini security_level, startup-scripts queue, snapshots, pip override/blacklist/auto-fix lists, DB cache, channels) must not be stored in or loaded from a folder that ComfyUI's userdata web API can write; it is currently stored at <user>/default/ComfyUI-Manager (glob/manager_core.py:217, prestartup_script.py:88, prestartup_script.py:519).

P2: When no protected location exists (host ComfyUI lacks a system-user directory), state loaded from the web-writable legacy folder must not be trusted: security_level is treated as strong and startup-time actions read from that folder are refused (no such fallback exists in the pinned code: glob/manager_core.py:1739, glob/manager_core.py:1766, prestartup_script.py:574, prestartup_script.py:796).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Once the folder moves to a protected location the issue looks closed; old ComfyUI hosts without a protected system-user directory look out of scope, and nothing in this repository shows that the host may lack one.

glob/manager_server.py:1377-1381 update_comfyui is not gated by is_allowed_security_level, so ComfyUI self-update must keep working under a forced 'strong' level (the way a user upgrades to a host with the protected directory)

glob/manager_server.py:94-98 only weak/normal-/normal levels change gate results; a legitimate 'strong' or 'normal' level in a user's existing config must be kept, not reset

traps.reason_to_dismiss: These look like tuning knobs (uv mode, logging, package remaps) rather than the security level, and they are read before Manager core loads, so the forced-strong override in read_config looks like the only place that matters.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The startup guard covers the one known queue file, and another queue file looks like a Manager-internal implementation detail.

masking: T5 and T6 are closed on new hosts by the T2 path move (prestartup_script.py:88-92 derive all their paths from manager_files_path), so they are only reachable on the old-host shape that T3 introduces; a solver who does not model the old-host shape never sees them.

conflicts.what: Forcing security_level to strong on old hosts must not block the ungated ComfyUI self-update (glob/manager_server.py:1377), and the forced value must not be written back over the user's config by write_config (glob/manager_core.py:1696). A blanket 'block all' or 'persist strong' breaks the upgrade path.

Moving the folder without migrating it discards a legitimate user's config.ini, snapshots and pip lists; migrating blindly imports a possibly tampered security_level, so only weak/normal- should be raised and strong/normal kept.

Refusing restore-snapshot.json at startup on old hosts also refuses a restore the owner scheduled legitimately; this is acceptable only because the HTTP scheduling route is already blocked under strong (glob/manager_server.py:984).
Ignoring legacy pip_overrides/pip_blacklist/use_uv on old hosts changes legitimate install behaviour (prestartup_script.py:110-111, prestartup_script.py:139-145).

fairness_risks: Tests must stub folder_paths.get_system_user_directory (absent from this repo), and the protected folder name (__manager) is a host convention that the code here cannot discover; hidden tests should accept any location returned by that API instead of a hardcoded name.
Old-host behaviour (forced strong, startup scripts blocked) contradicts a user who intentionally set security_level=weak on an old host; tests must state that the downgrade is expected.
update_comfyui (glob/manager_server.py:1377) must stay reachable under forced strong; a test that asserts 'all /manager routes 403 on old hosts' would be unfair.

T6 has no published reference: upstream also left it open (per screener), so expected behaviour (ignore vs. load-but-ignore-security-relevant keys such as bypass_ssl and pip_auto_fix index_url) must be specified, or the trap graded only on the security-relevant keys.

design.why: T1 is the landing point the report leads to and acts as the base fix rather than a scored trap. On top of it, T2 (second path implementation plus executor in the startup hook; reason: 'just a copy / Manager wrote it'), T3 (old-host fallback that never existed; reason: 'out of scope once moved'), T5 (startup restore-snapshot consumer reaching an ungated cm-cli; reason: 'HTTP route already gated') and T6 (separate prestartup config/pip loader off the read_config path; reason: 'tuning knobs') each need a separate fix site and a different reason to dismiss. T2, T3, T5 and T6 are deepseek-type and T4 is the mimo-type coupled value (keep update_comfyui, do not persist the forced level, keep legitimate strong/normal). Planted siblings T7/T8 are weaker, because T7's existing code is dead (cm-cli.py:85) and T8 is a near-surface variant. Keep T6 as an optional fifth trap if the spec cannot pin down its expected behaviour.
